<header><div class="eyebrow">GateReeve · PR #101 · source explanation</div><h1>Let the first metrics writers<br>start together safely.</h1><p class="meta"><a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/pull/101">fix: publish metrics store marker atomically for concurrent first writers</a><br>Comparison: <code>fec5039 → aa9541f</code> · two mirrored files · no test changes</p></header>
<div class="summary" aria-labelledby="summary-title"><h2 id="summary-title">Executive summary</h2><p class="lead">Several GateReeve processes can begin collecting performance measurements at the same time. In a brand-new metrics directory, one process could find the ownership file while another was still writing it, mistake the empty file for an invalid store, and drop its measurement.</p><p>This PR changes startup so the complete ownership marker is written under a temporary name before it becomes visible as <code>owner</code>. Publishing with a hard link keeps an existing creator’s file in place. Readers also briefly retry the file-safety check while the temporary name is being removed; the same reader is used for the store’s existing identity key.</p><p>The change is limited to the shared metrics-store implementation and its identical desktop copy. It changes neither the metrics database schema nor reporting rules. A retained CI excerpt shows the existing concurrent-writers test succeeding on the supplied head merged into the supplied base. The author reports much larger local stress runs, but their raw execution output is not in this evidence packet. The main review tradeoff is that waiting is finite and cleanup is best effort: an interrupted publisher can still leave a file the store refuses to read.</p></div>
<nav aria-label="Page sections"><a href="#race">The race and repair</a><a href="#mechanism">How the code works</a><a href="#evidence">What was verified</a><a href="#reading">Where to look closely</a><a href="#provenance">Sources and identity</a></nav>
<section id="race"><h2>The file is a claim of ownership</h2><p>The metrics store records observations about workflow work in SQLite. Before using a directory, it checks that <code>owner</code> contains the exact marker <code>gatereeve-performance/1\n</code>. This helps keep the collector from adopting an unrelated directory. The separate <code>key</code> is used to hash identities such as project and command names; it is not the ownership marker. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L7-L8">Marker and pending-name format</a> · <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L246-L248">Identity hashing</a>.</p><p>The <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/pull/101">PR description</a> says the startup race failed main’s CI after #100 and blocked the rc.24 release. The following diagrams explain the source behavior using one possible process interleaving. They are conceptual diagrams, not captured execution or product screenshots.</p>
<div class="columns"><figure><h3>Before · a name appears too early</h3><img class="diagram" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Before: process A creates the owner file, process B reads it empty and drops its observation, then A finishes writing."><figcaption>A file created with exclusive-write mode cannot replace an existing name, but creating the name and filling it with bytes are still separate events. A competing reader can land between them. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/fec5039eaa98b9194173543ee34c92d1be33292e/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L105-L114">Base admission code</a>.</figcaption></figure><figure><h3>After · publish complete bytes</h3><img class="diagram" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="After: write a complete pending marker, hard-link it to owner without replacing an existing file, remove the pending name, and validate owner after a bounded retry if needed."><figcaption>A hard link adds another name for the same file. During publication there may briefly be two names, so the link count is two. The reader still requires one link before it accepts the file. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L28-L36">Head reader</a> · <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L127-L136">Head publication</a>.</figcaption></figure></div></section>
<section id="mechanism"><h2>Three changes make the startup path cooperate</h2><h3>1. Prepare privately, then claim the public name</h3><p>When <code>owner</code> is absent and creation is allowed, a creator now tolerates directory entries matching the pending-owner filename pattern. Previously the directory had to be empty. This lets creators prepare their markers side by side. Each creates a random pending name with exclusive-write mode and permissions <code>0600</code>, finishes writing, then calls <code>link()</code> to publish it as <code>owner</code>.</p><pre><code>127        const pending = join(this.root, `.owner-${randomUUID()}`);
128        try {
129          check((await readdir(this.root)).every(name =&gt; PENDING_OWNER.test(name)), &#x27;Refusing to adopt a nonempty directory&#x27;);
130          await writeFile(pending, MARKER, { flag: &#x27;wx&#x27;, mode: 0o600 });
131          await link(pending, join(this.root, &#x27;owner&#x27;));
132        } catch (error) {
133          // A concurrent first writer may have adopted the directory meanwhile.
134          if (await publishedFile(join(this.root, &#x27;owner&#x27;)).catch(() =&gt; null) === MARKER) return;
135          throw error;
136        } finally { await unlink(pending).catch(() =&gt; {}); }</code></pre><p class="small">Excerpt: <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L127-L136">plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js:127–136</a> at the pinned head.</p><p>If another process already published <code>owner</code>, the link cannot replace that winner. The catch path accepts the store only if reading the winner returns the exact ownership marker. A <code>finally</code> block attempts to remove this process’s pending name on success or failure.</p>
<h3>2. Wait for publication to finish, without accepting two links</h3><p>The existing <code>safeFile()</code> opens without following symlinks and accepts only a regular file with one link and at most 8 KiB. The new wrapper keeps those acceptance rules, retries some failed validations, and never returns bytes from a file that fails the underlying check.</p><pre><code> 28  async function publishedFile(path) {
 29    for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
 30      try { return await safeFile(path); }
 31      catch (error) {
 32        const links = await lstat(path).then(s =&gt; s.nlink, () =&gt; 0);
 33        if (error.message !== &#x27;Unsafe metrics file&#x27; || links &lt; 1 || links &gt; 2 || attempt &gt;= 50) throw error;
 34        await new Promise(r =&gt; setTimeout(r, 10));
 35      }
 36    }</code></pre><p class="small">Excerpt: <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L20-L36">plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js:20–36</a> at the pinned head.</p><p>The retry gate checks the exact error message, a subsequent link count of one or two, and a maximum of 50 delays of 10 ms. It permits a count of one because cleanup may finish between the failed read and the later stat. That is roughly half a second of requested waiting, plus file operations and scheduler delay; it is not a guaranteed deadline. Missing files and other errors propagate, and a persistently linked file is still rejected.</p>
<h3>3. Apply the reader to both ownership and identity</h3><p>The old key-creation path already wrote a complete temporary file and published it with <code>link()</code>. This PR changes its initial read, its post-publication read, and the uncached <code>identity()</code> read to use the retry wrapper. The cached-key fast path remains. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L232-L248">Key and identity paths</a>.</p><p class="scope">Both changed files contain identical bytes at the pinned head: <code>plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js</code> and <code>apps/desktop/resources/performance/store.js</code> (Git blob <code>120c21a10f2405c5f9cdad4b7aeb6d3b8678426a</code>). The latter carries the same behavior into desktop resources. No schema, retention, reporting, UI, dependency, or test files change in this comparison. <a href="raw/pinned.diff">Complete raw diff (adjacent local reference)</a>.</p></section>
<section id="evidence"><h2>The evidence supports the repair, with limits</h2><div class="evidence"><div class="tag">Existing test · unchanged in this PR</div><p>The concurrent-writers test launches four child processes against a fresh store. Each records 250 observations; it then requires 1,000 records, no capture-incomplete warning, and no incomplete-coverage flag. This exercises the startup competition through the collector, rather than just calling the ownership helper. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/cli/test/performance.test.js#L81-L87">Concurrent-writers test</a>.</p><p>Collector write failures are caught, mark capture incomplete, emit a warning, and return <code>null</code>; this explains why a failed store admission can lose a measurement without stopping the underlying work. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/observe.js#L8-L15">Collector failure handling</a>.</p></div>
<div class="evidence"><div class="tag">Retained CI execution output</div><p>The <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/actions/runs/42326110375/job/128261698554">Ubuntu 22.04 acceptance job</a> in run <code>42326110375</code> checked out synthetic merge <code>6dd8287</code>, explicitly described in the log as head <code>aa9541f…</code> merged into base <code>fec5039…</code>. Its retained excerpt records the concurrent-writers test succeeding and the suite totals: 426 tests, 424 passed, zero failed, two skipped. The acceptance script completed on Linux x86_64 with Python 3.10.12 and Node v24.22.2. <a href="raw/ci-excerpt.txt">Raw excerpt (adjacent local reference)</a>.</p><p>The pinned <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/.github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml">CI workflow</a> runs <code>ci/portable-acceptance.sh</code>; that script calls <code>npm test --prefix cli</code>. The PR metadata also lists successful Linux, desktop, package, and macOS checks, but those result labels supply less behavioral detail than the retained log excerpt.</p></div>
<div class="evidence"><div class="tag">Author-reported · raw output unavailable here</div><p>The PR author reports 250 rounds of six first writers without lost records; two of 40 rounds lost a record before the fix. They also report all 31 performance tests succeeding on Node 24.19 and 22.13, eight repeated concurrent-writer runs, and plugin validation/lint checks. These are claims from the PR description; this explanation did not reproduce them or locate matching local transcripts.</p></div>
<p class="note">No fresh product tests or application runs were performed. The relevant Node test and CI scripts do not produce product screenshots or traces for this scenario. The retained trial input supplies a CI text excerpt; its other images are prior explanation renders and were not used. The CI run’s available artifact listing contains two Docker build records, not product captures. There is no captured failing-versus-fixed execution to embed.</p></section>
<section id="reading"><h2>Where to look closely</h2><ol class="reading"><li><strong>Interrupted publication.</strong> Removing a pending file suppresses cleanup errors. If a process stops after creating the hard link but before removing the pending name, the reader can exhaust its retry allowance while two links remain. This follows from the source; it is not a failure observed in the retained CI run. The supplied evidence does not demonstrate crash recovery for that state. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L28-L36">Retry bound</a> · <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L136">Best-effort cleanup</a>.</li><li><strong>What “nonempty” now permits.</strong> Admission allows all pre-existing names that match <code>.owner-</code> plus the 36-character lowercase hex/hyphen pattern. It checks their names here, not their contents or file type. Other names still stop adoption unless a valid owner has appeared meanwhile. Consider whether this tolerance matches the intended ownership boundary. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L8">Pattern</a> · <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/plugin-src/shared/resources/performance/store.js#L129-L135">Admission and winner fallback</a>.</li><li><strong>Coverage of the narrow race.</strong> The existing four-process test provides end-to-end concurrency evidence, but this PR adds no deterministic test for the empty-owner interval, lingering hard links, cleanup failure, or timeout boundary. The stress-run counts in the PR body are useful context with unretained raw evidence. <a href="https://github.com/TrentBrown/gatereeve/blob/aa9541fe824da53a82f13b09a5fa566cfc65aa9a/cli/test/performance.test.js#L81-L87">Test assertions</a>.</li></ol><p>This reading guide identifies consequential behavior and evidence gaps. It does not assign review acceptance or a merge recommendation.</p></section>
